title: Precision Recommendations from Molecular tumor boards and their cllnical implementation in neuro-oncology: a real-world regiStry and Evaluation (PROMISE)
summary:
Modern genetic testing can identify alterations in tumours of the brain and nervous system that may provide additional treatment options. At specialised multidisciplinary tumour board meetings, physicians review these findings and recommend individual treatment approaches.

The PROMISE study investigates how often such recommendations are actually implemented in routine clinical care and which factors may prevent their implementation. It also examines the genetic alterations identified and the subsequent disease course and health outcomes of affected patients.

PROMISE is a single-centre observational registry. Previously collected medical data are analysed retrospectively, followed by planned prospective inclusion of additional eligible patients.

The study does not alter patient treatment and requires no additional examinations or treatments solely for research purposes.
conditions: Secondary malignant neoplasm of kidney and renal pelvis

interventions.name:
Adult neuro-oncology patients (≥18 years) discussed at a molecular tumour board with available molecular pathological testing. Eligible cases are included retrospectively from 1 January 2023, followed by consecutive prospective enrolment during the planned five-year study period.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Neuro-oncological disease, including primary central nervous system tumours or secondary CNS involvement from systemic malignancies.

Case presentation at the Molecular Tumour Board (MTB) of University Hospital Düsseldorf.

Availability of molecular pathological testing performed as part of routine clinical care.

Retrospective cohort: MTB presentation on or after 1 January 2023 and availability of the required minimum clinical and molecular pathological dataset.

Prospective cohort: Valid written informed consent for the scientific use of clinical and molecular data obtained within the existing MTB/genomic sequencing workflow.

Patients are eligible irrespective of whether a therapeutic MTB recommendation is issued or a molecularly targeted treatment is subsequently initiated.
Exclusion criteria:
Age below 18 years at the relevant MTB presentation or registry inclusion.

No presentation at the Molecular Tumour Board of University Hospital Düsseldorf.

Absence of molecular pathological testing.

Insufficient minimum clinical or molecular pathological data preventing evaluation of essential study parameters in the retrospective cohort.

Documented objection to scientific use of health data or absence of an applicable legal basis for retrospective secondary data use.

Prospective cohort: Missing or withdrawn valid written informed consent for scientific data use.

Missing individual follow-up variables or unavailable patient-reported outcomes do not automatically result in exclusion if the required minimum dataset is available.
